4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 2

Present simple: affirmative and negative

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use the present simple for habits and facts (costumbres y verdades)
  • Add -s or -es with he, she and it
  • Make negative sentences with don't and doesn't
  • Write true sentences about you and your family

Para pensar

En inglés decimos «I play», «you play», «we play»… pero «she plays». ¿De dónde sale esa s?

Explicación

When do we use it?

We use the present simple for things that happen again and again (habits): «I walk to school every day», «We play football on Saturdays». We also use it for things that are always true (facts): «Cows eat grass», «The sun rises in the east».

En castellano: es como nuestro presente cuando hablamos de costumbres: «como fruta todos los días», «los gatos duermen mucho». No sirve para lo que está pasando justo ahora; para eso hay otro tiempo que verás más adelante.

I, you, we, they: easy!

With I, you, we and they, the verb doesn't change. It's the same word you find in the dictionary: «I like apples», «You like apples», «We like apples», «They like apples».

This is great news! In Spanish we say «me gusta, te gusta, nos gusta…», with different endings. In English, for four persons, the verb is exactly the same. Remember that you means «tú» and also «vosotros»: «You live in Bilbao» can be one person or a group.

He, she, it: add -s

With he, she and it we add -s to the verb: «He plays the guitar», «She reads comics», «It rains a lot in Galicia».

This also happens with names and with one person or thing: «Marta swims», «My dad cooks», «The dog barks». A good trick: if you can change the subject for he, she or it, put the -s. En castellano: piensa en la «s» como una pegatina que solo llevan él, ella y ello.

Spelling: -s, -es, -ies

Most verbs just add -s: play → plays, like → likes, eat → eats. But verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x and -o add -es: watch → watches, wash → washes, go → goes, do → does.

Verbs ending in consonant + y change to -ies: study → studies, fly → flies. But if there is a vowel before the y, just add -s: play → plays. And one special verb: have → has. «She has a brother.»

Negative: don't

To say no, we put don't (do not) before the verb: «I don't like spiders», «We don't go to school on Sunday», «They don't eat meat».

We use don't with I, you, we, they. En castellano: es nuestro «no»: «no me gustan las arañas». Pero fíjate: en inglés no basta con poner not delante («I not like»), necesitamos la palabrita ayudante do. Es como un amigo que viene a ayudar al verbo cuando decimos que no.

Negative: doesn't

With he, she, it the helper changes to doesn't (does not): «She doesn't like spiders», «My cat doesn't eat vegetables», «It doesn't snow in Seville».

Very important: the -s goes to doesn't, so the verb loses its -s. We say «He doesn't play», never «He doesn't plays». En castellano: la «s» no puede estar dos veces. Si ya la lleva does, el verbo vuelve a su forma normal.

Time words

The present simple often comes with time words that show repetition: every day (todos los días), every week, on Mondays (los lunes), at the weekend (el fin de semana), in summer.

They usually go at the end of the sentence: «I have English on Tuesdays», «We go to the beach in summer». En castellano: fíjate que en inglés los días de la semana se escriben siempre con mayúscula: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday… ¡En español no!

Reading: my family's habits

Read Daniel's text: «My family is very busy. My mum works in a hospital. She starts work at seven. My dad teaches maths. He doesn't drive to work: he goes by bus. My sister Ana studies a lot and she plays the piano. I don't play the piano, but I love football. We all have dinner together at eight. My grandpa lives with us and he watches the news every night.»

Find three verbs with -s, one with -es and one with -ies. Who doesn't drive?

Let's practise: true or false?

Play this game in pairs. Write four sentences about your partner, two affirmative and two negative: «Carla likes cats», «Carla doesn't eat fish». Then read them aloud. Your partner says «True!» or «False!» and corrects you: «False! I don't like cats. I like dogs».

Consejo: antes de leer, revisa cada frase. Si el sujeto es él o ella, ¿lleva el verbo la s? En las negativas con doesn't, ¿has quitado la s del verbo? Si lo haces bien, ¡ganas un punto!

Present simple

Ejercicios

  1. Write the -s form: read, swim, cook.

  2. Write the -es form: wash, go, catch.

  3. Write the third person: study, cry, play.

  4. Complete: «My brother ___ (have) a bike.»

  5. Complete with don't or doesn't: «We ___ like rain.»

  6. Complete with don't or doesn't: «The baby ___ walk.»

  7. Make it negative: «Lola speaks French.»

  8. Correct: «He don't watch TV.»

  9. Translate: «Mi gato duerme en el sofá.»

  10. Write two true sentences about a friend (one negative).

Practica

  1. «She ___ comics.»

    1. A) read
    2. B) reades
    3. C) reads

  2. «They ___ in Valencia.»

    1. A) live
    2. B) lives
    3. C) livs

  3. The -s form of «watch» is…

    1. A) watchs
    2. B) watches
    3. C) watchies

  4. The -s form of «study» is…

    1. A) studys
    2. B) studies
    3. C) studyes

  5. «He ___ a sister.»

    1. A) haves
    2. B) have
    3. C) has

  6. «I ___ like spiders.»

    1. A) don't
    2. B) doesn't
    3. C) not

  7. «My dog ___ eat apples.»

    1. A) don't
    2. B) isn't
    3. C) doesn't

  8. Which is correct?

    1. A) He doesn't plays.
    2. B) He doesn't play.
    3. C) He don't play.

  9. We use the present simple for…

    1. A) habits
    2. B) what is happening now
    3. C) the past

  10. Which is written correctly?

    1. A) on Monday
    2. B) on monday
    3. C) On monday

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el presente simple; Por qué el verbo lleva -s con he, she, it; Las reglas de -s, -es, -ies y el verbo has; Cómo se forma la negativa con don't y doesn't.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

present simpleCostumbres y verdades: I walk to school.
he / she / it + sShe plays. It rains.
-eswatch → watches · go → goes.
-iesstudy → studies.
have → hasShe has a dog.
don'tNo (I, you, we, they).
doesn'tNo (he, she, it); el verbo sin s.
on MondaysLos lunes (con mayúscula).

Soluciones

  1. C) she + s.
  2. A) they sin s.
  3. B) -ch + es.
  4. B) consonante + y → ies.
  5. C) have → has.
  6. A) I + don't.
  7. C) dog = it.
  8. B) Sin s tras doesn't.
  9. A) Costumbres.
  10. A) Días con mayúscula.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. reads, swims, cooks.
  2. washes, goes, catches.
  3. studies, cries, plays.
  4. has.
  5. don't.
  6. doesn't.
  7. Lola doesn't speak French.
  8. He doesn't watch TV.
  9. My cat sleeps on the sofa.
  10. Model answer: Hugo likes basketball. He doesn't like milk.
